conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be your doctor during this stay. You were admitted for rib pain, correct?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I lifted a heavy bag and now my left side hurts badly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We reviewed your chest X-ray. No fracture, but the area is tender. We’ll treat it as musculoskeletal pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, but I also have terrible abdominal pain. It’s constant and worse lately.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see you have a complex GI history. You're on a pain contract and taking morphine at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, but it’s not enough. I need IV Dilaudid. I’ve had it before during admissions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I’ve consulted pain management. Dilaudid can worsen your bowel motility, which is already very slow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: But I need relief. Without it, I can’t function. I’ll leave if I don’t get it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand you're in pain, but we can’t give IV Dilaudid. It could cause a bowel blockage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Then I’m leaving. I can’t stay here without proper pain control.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll discharge you with your home meds and the Lidoderm patch for your rib. Are you safe to go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Fine. But I’m not okay. I’m going to kill myself when I get home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I need to take that seriously. We’ll get Psychiatry to see you right away.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Psychiatry has evaluated you. They’re concerned and want to keep you for observation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t want to be here if I can’t have Dilaudid. I pulled my femoral line. I thought I’d bleed to death.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We saw that. There was minimal bleeding, but it’s a serious act. You’re now on a 1:1 sitter for safety.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Still in pain. And I need my femoral line replaced. I can’t eat. I need TPN.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve been watching. You’ve been seen eating and drinking. Nutrition did a calorie count.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I can’t keep food down. I’m nauseous all the time. I need the line.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The count showed you’re taking in about 68% of calories and 29% of protein. It’s low, but not critical.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: But I can’t live like this. I need the line replaced. And I need IV pain meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your GI doctor reviewed your case. He doesn’t feel the line is needed right now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Then I’ll just keep saying I want to die until someone listens.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We take your words seriously. That’s why you’re on a sitter and seeing Psychiatry daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did an upper GI study with Gastrografin. The contrast reached your cecum in 45 minutes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So? I still can’t eat.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The study shows no blockage. Your bowel is moving things through, just slowly. It’s stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: But I need the femoral line. I have no other access.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We understand, but without a medical need, we can’t replace it. We can use oral or rectal meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: They don’t work. Only IV works. You’re not helping me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve had a few episodes where you arch your back and moan. Neurology thinks they may be pseudoseizures.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: They’re not fake. I’ve been evaluated. I have real seizures.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep following with Neurology. But during the episodes, you respond to touch.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I can’t control them. And I’m still in pain. Why won’t you give me Dilaudid?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Because it could stop your bowels completely. You’ve had obstructions before. It’s too risky.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs are stable. White count is low but not concerning. Kidney and liver function are okay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I still feel awful. And I’m not eating because I’m nauseous.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve seen you eat meals. We believe you can maintain nutrition without the femoral line for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: You don’t believe me. I need IV meds and my line back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Psychiatry says your suicidal thoughts have decreased. You haven’t mentioned self-harm today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m still in pain. But I guess I won’t say I want to die anymore.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re glad. And your pain seems at baseline. The Lidoderm patch is helping your rib.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: But my belly pain is still there. You’re not fixing it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve done all we can safely. No new blockage, no infection. We can’t give IV Dilaudid.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re discharging you today. You’re medically stable. Your mental state has improved.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I still don’t feel better. But I’ll go.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll go home with your regular meds. Morphine PR for pain, and we’ve adjusted your Lovenox dose.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No IV access? No Dilaudid?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No. But we’ve spoken with your GI and pain doctors. Follow up with them soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Fine. I’ll call them.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: And please reach out if you feel unsafe. You’re not alone.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know. I won’t do anything. I just want to feel heard.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We hear you. This is complex, and we’re coordinating with your team. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you for not giving up on me, even when I was angry.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Of course. Your safety is our priority. We’ll be here if you need us.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll follow up with my doctors. I promise.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s all we ask. You’re strong, and you’ve gotten through a tough time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel a little more hope today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re glad. Take it one day at a time. You’re going home with a clear mind and safe plan.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m ready to go home now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll get the discharge papers ready. Rest, stay hydrated, and call if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care of yourself.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll try.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s all anyone can do. We believe in you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I appreciate that.
